questions.stem: Why does diamond have a very high melting point?

options.text: Because it contains ionic bonds
Because each carbon atom forms four strong covalent bonds in a giant structure, requiring a lot of energy to break
Because it contains delocalised electrons
Because it has weak intermolecular forces

questions.explanation: Diamond has a very high melting point because it is a giant covalent structure where each carbon atom is bonded to four others by strong covalent bonds. A huge amount of energy is needed to break these many strong bonds.

options.text: Because it is made of carbon, which is a strong element
Because it has a rigid three-dimensional structure with strong covalent bonds throughout
Because it contains metallic bonds
Because the atoms are very close together

questions.explanation: Diamond's hardness comes from its rigid three-dimensional tetrahedral structure where each carbon atom forms four strong covalent bonds. This creates an extremely rigid and strong structure.

questions.stem: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?

options.text: Because graphite contains ions
Because graphite has delocalised electrons that can move between layers
Because diamond has stronger bonds
Because graphite is a metal

questions.explanation: In graphite, each carbon forms only 3 covalent bonds, leaving one electron per atom delocalised. These free electrons can move along the layers and carry electrical charge. In diamond, all four electrons are used in bonding.

questions.stem: Why is graphite soft and slippery?

options.text: Because it has weak covalent bonds
Because the layers are held together by weak intermolecular forces and can slide over each other
Because it contains water between the layers
Because it has a low melting point

questions.explanation: Graphite consists of layers of carbon atoms. Within each layer, bonds are strong, but the layers are held together only by weak intermolecular forces. This allows layers to slide over each other easily.

questions.stem: Silicon dioxide (SiO₂) has a very high melting point. What type of structure does it have?

options.text: Simple molecular
Giant ionic
Giant covalent
Metallic

questions.explanation: Silicon dioxide has a giant covalent structure similar to diamond, with each silicon atom bonded to four oxygen atoms in a continuous three-dimensional network. This explains its very high melting point.

questions.stem: How many covalent bonds does each carbon atom form in diamond?
questions.explanation: In diamond, each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds in a tetrahedral arrangement. This uses all four of carbon's outer electrons.

questions.stem: How many covalent bonds does each carbon atom form in graphite?
questions.explanation: In graphite, each carbon atom forms three covalent bonds with other carbon atoms in flat hexagonal layers. The fourth outer electron becomes delocalised between the layers.
